description:
`:erlang.abs(-3)` compiles as field access and fails at runtime (fz_struct_get_named_field_ref: ExpectedTag). Cause: decode makes (".",2) an Expr::Index; direct_callee (jobs/body.rs:4435) and CallableName::from_expr (src/ast/mod.rs:62) accept only Var/Module/Index chains, so an Expr::Atom base falls through to FieldAccess (body.rs:1345).

Decision (2026-10-17): atom module names, as in Elixir where a module's identity is an atom. Module paths may be a single atom; `defmodule :erlang` parses (parse_module/parse_upper_path, frontdoor.rs:292,1647, accept Tok::Atom); an atom-based remote call resolves through the same module lookup; an unknown `:foo.bar()` gets a diagnostic naming :foo. lib/erlang.fz defines :erlang with float_to_binary/2 and decimals: N (fixed notation, correctly rounded, as Rust format!("{:.*}", n, x)); runtime extern via alloc_text (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1142).
title: `:atom.fun(args)` is a remote call; :erlang.float_to_binary/2
